Beast, orphan and refugee from one of the Bandit Kingdoms, was one of the best gunners at boot camp, but the worst at poker.
Hawk prides himself on his ability to swoop in for the kill and in the fact that he can make any minor skirmish sound like an epic battle.
Self-named and a crack shot, it is Siren who most often walks away from the poker table with Beast's paycheck.
Born and raised on a backwater world of the Lyran Commonwealth, Rooster can steer a `Mech through the tightest terrain.
Cool under fire, Isis earned high marks in training for battlefield awareness.
Gunman enjoys living up to his name. He's happiest with an Alpha Strike.
Mystique won't talk about her history, but no one questions her ability to make a `Mech all but fly.
Few in training could match Skater's ability to pilot a `Mech, but far fewer appreciated his sense of humor.
Spice's all-around athleticism helps her muscle even the toughest of `Mechs (and MechWarriors) into place.
Distantly related by blood to the ruling Davion family, Baron and his sister Countess consider it their duty, honor, and right to fight the Jaguars.
Don't let the name fool you, Fiend is anything but. He'll even lend you money, at a reasonable rate, if you need it.
Of distant Kurita descent, Ronin fought hard to get transferred to the Davion Guards when the first rumors of a counter-attack surfaced.
Prone to midday naps, Gator is none-the-less the man you need when that last, desperate shot has to count.
A Steiner-loyalist, Rebel wears that badge and her Maneuver Training citation with pride.
With a well chosen call-sign, Hunter knows how to move and shoot like few others.
Sly and wily, Lynx welcomes the chance to jump his `Mech into places he shouldn't be. Fortunately he has the gunnery skills to save his own skin.
A crack-shot and decent with sensors, Hitman welcomes the chance to pay back the Smoke Jaguars for their crimes.
Like her younger brother Baron, Countess views herself as one of the noble elite who believe themselves destined to regain the lost Davion glory.
A techno-fiend, Scarab has his 'Mech's sensors and target-assistance electronics hot-wired to the frying point.
Outlaw entered the Davion military as an infantry grunt, but through luck and no little talent has earned himself a ride with the best of the best.
Though her family name carries great weight in the Davion military, Falcon fights continuously to insure that she's treated no differently than anyone else.
Tired of getting shot down, Burnout transferred from the aerospace corps to where the real action is. So far he hasn't been disappointed.
Goblin is prepared to make any Smoke Jaguar he meets pay for the collective crimes of all the Clans. Fortunately, he has the ability to back that up.
Mantis fought the Clans in the original invasion and has vowed not to let them get the better of her again.
An avowed Kurita-phile, Dragon has been reviewing Clan tactics and is more than ready to take the battle to them.
Though she's mellowed of late, Blaze is infamous for demanding the best of everything. The truth is, however, she's earned it.
A Davion veteran, Thunder transferred from a command position in his old unit to get a crack at the Jaguars.
A near legend among Inner Sphere forces, Paingod's goal is to pilot a captured Clan OmniMech into battle against them.
Put him at the controls of an assault-class BattleMech and you will understand the reason for his call-sign, Firestorm.
Vixen's fought more battles than nearly anyone in the Davion Guard, and she's never seen the white of a cockpit parachute.
Raised on an isolated Periphery world, Boomer's dialect is more than difficult to understand. Fortunately, he lets his `Mech do most of the talking.
You won't find this MechWarrior in the barracks- Detox's `Mech is his home. Unfortunately, that means the cleaning crews get hazard pay...
Quiet and aloof without tons of hardened metal around her, Ghost comes alive on the battlefield. Even then, however, she's one of the more reserved in the unit.
Her nickname comes not from the effect she has on teammates, but on the bad luck that seems to fall on the enemy when she's around.
A military brat, Needle knows nothing but military life. But, unlike her siblings, she has no intention or pursuing promotion. She prefers the trenches.
Pyro earned his name for reasons you can well imagine. His obsession, however, aptly conceals a sharp military mind and professional warrior.
Sponge owns nothing that he did not beg, borrow, or steal from someone. Even his callsign, believe it or not, is lifted from someone in the Wolf Dragoons.
Squid's callsign is a holdover from his days as a green MechWarrior. A rookie no longer, Squid is looking forward to testing his mettle against the Clans.
The veteran Toad is even grumpier out of the cockpit than in. To that end, his superiors try and assign him to picket duty whenever practical.
To many, it seems amazing that Vandal has lived as long as he has. If there is a risk to be taken on the battlefield, he charges to it.
Wasp loves recon work, the lighter and faster the `Mech the better. Fortunately, few can pilot a speeding 25-ton piece of metal as she can.
With many combats under her belt, Spice has learned that brute force isn't always the answer and a careful, precise touch sometimes wins the day.
With his exploits against the Smoke Jaguars broadcast on his homeplanet's newsvids, Baron has become even more insufferable than ever.
Fiend has discovered the spare parts market and has been taking personal interest in the inventory of equipment recovered from enemy `Mechs he's destroyed.
Despite the victories against the Smoke Jaguars, Ronin has found himself missing the life and culture of the Draonic Combine more and more.
Some in the unit want Gator to change his name to Trickshot in recognition of his ability to make the tough shot when it's needed most.
Time with a hard-core Davion unit has dulled Rebel's Steiner patriotism somewhat, but it's still strong enough to provoke the occasional fist fight...
Hitman has been very happy helping to grind the Smoke Jaguars into the ground. Unfortunately, some of his unit-mates fear it's becoming an obsession.
Burnout enjoys `Mech piloting more than he ever did aeropspace jockeying, but now understands the value of being high and above the fray.

text: The Bulldog is a slow, tough short-range damage machine packing a heavy autocannon.
The Condor is a well-balanced medium-range tank firing a large pulse laser.
The Harasser is a durable short-range combat mounting SRM packs. Its drivers use its speed to advantage by making quick, strafing runs and then moving to safety.
The J. Edgar is a lightly armored quick-strike tank firing pulse lasers. When operating in a group, its drivers favor a circling tactic that distracts the enemy.
The LRM carrier is a dangerous, lightly armored missile boat firing LRM racks.
The Minelayer is a defensive unit designed to delay and funnel enemy movement.
The Minesweeper clears a path through a minefield by safely detonating enemy mines. Each mine it safely detonates, however, reduces the vehicle's capability.
The Pegasus is an armed scout vehicle equipped with sensors.
The Refit Truck makes field repairs to BattleMech armor and replenishes expended ammunition.
The Rommel is a thickly armored, medium-range heavy-strike tank firing twin autocannons.
The Saracen is a fast long-range strike vehicle firing light autocannons. When operating in groups, their pilots tend to concentrate fire and then move on to the next victim.
The Savannah Master is an exceedingly high speed short-range fighter with poor armor. This vehicle moves in packs that swarm a target, impeding its ability to escape.
Though it moves slowly, beware the Shrek's multiple ER-PPCs. Beware! When this vehicle stops, it's about to fire!
The SRM carrier is a quick, lightly armored missile boat firing multiple SRM packs. It tends to move in for a close-range volley and then back off while the SRMs reload.
The Striker is a long-range missile tank capable of taking and inflicting serious damage.
The Swiftwind is an unarmed, lightly armored scout vehicle equipped with sensors.
The Von Luckner is a heavily armored, long-range assault vehicle firing a light autocannon and a gauss rifle. Beware! When this vehicle stops, it's about to fire!
This fast, heavily armed scout car is equipped with Guardian Electronic Countermeasures and advanced vehicle sensors.
This swift and agile tank carries a massive gauss rifle capable of devastating most targets with one shot. It can use its speed to bring that weapon to bear on weak rear `Mech armor.
The Manticore is a heavy tank carrying excellent armor protection and effective long and medium-range firepower.
This version of the Pilum Heavy Tank trades some of its firepower for a larger powerplant, making it faster than any vehicle in its weight class.
A Star League era design, the Alacorn MKIV packs reasonable speed, superior armor, and a terrifying punch into one sleek package.
The Ammo Truck is an inexpensive, reasonably fast, explosive vehicle capable of replacing a 'Mech's ammunition but not armor. Command it like the Refit Truck.
